OMP THIRD-PARTY NOTICES
=======================

This generated, self-contained aggregate accompanies OMP release artifacts.
It does not replace package-level license files. First-party licensing grants
no rights in third-party code, fonts, data, or marks identified below.

PYTHON DEPENDENCY DISTRIBUTION ROLE
===================================

omp-rpc has no third-party runtime dependencies. robomp declares FastAPI,
Uvicorn, HTTPX, Pydantic, pydantic-settings, python-dotenv, Click, and omp-rpc
as ordinary installer-resolved dependencies. The Python wheels do not vendor
those projects; each dependency remains a separately installed distribution
carrying its own license metadata and files. Container/system assemblers must
retain those independently installed distributions' notices.

TRACKED VENDORED CODE AND ASSET NOTICES
=======================================

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
crates/vendor/brush-core/LICENSE

This directory contains a vendored, locally-patched copy of brush-core from the
brush shell project (https://github.com/reubeno/brush), used under the MIT
License. It is wired into the workspace via `[patch.crates-io]` so these
modifications can be maintained against the published release (brush-core
0.5.0).

  Copyright (c) 2024 reuben olinsky

Local modifications include: Windows path handling fixes (drive-alias and
rooted-path normalization in globs), an async background-PID fix for the nohup
wrapper, treating `/dev/null` as poll-ready to avoid an infinite poll on macOS,
and indentation/formatting standardization. The remaining logic tracks upstream
so behavior matches the published crate.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
crates/pi-builtins/LICENSE

This crate began as a locally-patched copy of brush-builtins from the brush shell
project (https://github.com/reubeno/brush), used under the MIT License, and still
tracks it for the POSIX/bash builtins.

  Copyright (c) 2024 reuben olinsky

Local modifications to the upstream builtins include: implementing
previously-stubbed builtins, the `wait` builtin (PID targeting plus the
`-f`/`-n`/`-p` flags), and cancellation support for the `read` builtin via poll.

It additionally hosts the in-process command-line utility builtins (`src/host.rs`
plus one module per command). Those are ports of third-party programs, previously
carried as separate vendored crates and now consolidated here; the host plumbing
is ours, the utility logic is theirs. Their notices are reproduced in full
below.

crates/pi-shell/NOTICE

This file documents third-party attribution for the shell-output minimizer in
this crate, which adapts an algorithm from RTK (https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk),
used under the MIT License.

  Copyright (c) the RTK authors (rtk-ai/rtk)

Adapted component: the `build_pytest_summary` algorithm from the upstream
`src/cmds/python/pytest_cmd.rs` (pinned at commit
878af7de99e0ba71da2e8fd996f6b52a1836e06c), re-implemented here in
`src/minimizer/filters/python.rs` as the pytest state machine (`filter_pytest`,
`pytest_success`, `is_pytest_*`, `looks_like_pytest_summary_part`). It preserves
failures, errors, and the final summary line; strips header framing, progress
dots, and verbose `PASSED` rows; and falls through unchanged on unknown-state
lines (RTK's defensive default) so xdist `[gwN]` prefixes and custom reporters
never cause data loss.

packages/utils/src/vendor/mermaid-ascii/NOTICE

This directory contains an in-house Mermaid-diagram-to-ASCII renderer adapted
from beautiful-mermaid (https://github.com/lukilabs/beautiful-mermaid), used
under the MIT License.

  Copyright (c) 2026 Craft Docs

Only the ASCII rendering pipeline is ported (flowchart/state, sequence, class,
ER, and xychart diagrams); the SVG renderer and its `elkjs` graph-layout
dependency, the browser entry point, and the SVG theme/style modules were
dropped. Terminal display width is reimplemented on `Bun.stringWidth`, and
inline label formatting (HTML tags, markdown emphasis) is reduced to plain text
for ASCII output. Layout and edge-routing logic is preserved faithfully so
ASCII output matches the upstream package.

BUN / NPM DEPENDENCY INVENTORY
==============================
This inventory is traversed from bun.lock, not from the host node_modules tree.
The locked all-target package names remain stable when a platform leaf is not
installed on this host. Package license and NOTICE/ThirdPartyNotices payloads
are read from the frozen install; generation fails explicitly when an
unreviewed source payload is unavailable.

SCOPED NON-PERMISSIVE PACKAGES
------------------------------
The exact @img/sharp-libvips-* 1.2.4 all-target family is LGPL-3.0-or-later. It is not distributed in OMP npm bundles or standalone assets: @huggingface/transformers is always external, installed into a user-side versioned runtime on demand, and sharp is stubbed for speech/text. The dynamically loaded native library remains replaceable. Corresponding source is available from https://github.com/lovell/sharp-libvips.git and upstream libvips sources.

lightningcss 1.32.0 and its exact target leaves are MPL-2.0 build-only dependencies. MPL is not globally allowed and these packages are absent from runtime artifacts.
